evidence: Narrowed to the summarizer's own native session; subagent transcript eligibility is not established. CURRENT-DESIGN.md:7 says native sessions occupy clones; :32-34 makes the summarizer an ordinary seat, automatically activates an absent occupant for transcript work, and tracks transcript coverage. DESIGN-NOTES.md:241 proposes observing session closure; :247-259 approves automatic activation and durable processing, but lists closure detection and retry details without a rule selecting eligible source sessions. I searched all four reviewed documents for eligibility, exclusions, source filters, self-processing, and stopping boundaries; none supplies an equivalent. Conditional failure path: if the summarizer's own closed session qualifies, its completion produces another processing request, which can activate a new occupant after the previous one leaves; the next session can repeat the cycle. This conflicts with bounded, useful dormant-seat operation (SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:93) and the stated processing purpose. It is an acknowledged design-stage gap, not a claim of an inevitable runtime loop or implemented failure; an explicit finite eligibility policy is needed before this workflow is specified.
